stemMd: A body displaces 0.003 m³ of water when fully submerged. Take water density as 1000 kg m⁻³ and g = 10 m s⁻². What is the buoyant force?
explanationMd: Archimedes’ principle gives buoyant force equal to the weight of displaced fluid: ρVg. Here the displaced mass is 1000 × 0.003 = 3 kg and its weight is 30 N. The object’s own mass is not needed for this force.

distractorRationale.c: This omits the factor g after finding displaced mass.
distractorRationale.d: This introduces an extra factor of ten.
distractorRationale.b: This mishandles the cubic-metre volume conversion.
distractorRationale.a: This does not use the actual displaced volume.
